title: Can Elderly Parents Claim Maintenance From Their Children?
desc: Parents unable to support themselves can claim up to Rs 10,000 a month from children through a Maintenance Tribunal, in Haldwani and Nainital too.
keywords: Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act parents
why: Many elderly parents in Uttarakhand's hill towns are left without support when children move away for work or stop providing for them, and the law gives them a faster remedy than an ordinary civil suit.
keyPoints: Parents and senior citizens unable to maintain themselves can claim monthly maintenance from their children under the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007.
The application goes to a Maintenance Tribunal headed by the Sub-Divisional Magistrate, not a civil court, and the Tribunal can order up to Rs 10,000 a month.
A parent need not be 60 to claim; only a person claiming as a 'senior citizen' for their own support must meet that age.
If a child was given property on a promise to look after the parent and breaks that promise, the Tribunal can declare the transfer void.

sections.h: Who can claim maintenance from children in Uttarakhand, and how much?
p: A parent or senior citizen who cannot maintain himself or herself out of their own income or property can claim monthly maintenance from their children under section 4 of the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007. The application is filed before the Maintenance Tribunal, headed by the Sub-Divisional Magistrate, in the district where the parent lives, including Haldwani and Nainital. The Tribunal can order maintenance of up to Rs 10,000 a month.

A childless senior citizen can also claim maintenance from a relative who possesses their property or stands to inherit it. The Act keeps 'parent' and 'senior citizen' as separate terms: a parent of any age, including a stepparent, can apply, while someone relying only on the 'senior citizen' category must be 60 or older.

Hindu parents have a second route. Section 20 of the Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956 obliges a Hindu to maintain aged or infirm parents who cannot support themselves; that claim is enforced through a civil suit rather than the Tribunal.

sections.h: How does the Tribunal process work, and can a property gift be undone?
p: An application can be made by the parent, by someone authorised to act for them, by a registered voluntary organisation, or the Tribunal can act on its own. The Tribunal holds a summary inquiry rather than a full trial, which is meant to make the process quicker than an ordinary maintenance suit.

Section 23 of the 2007 Act protects parents who transfer property to a child or relative on condition that they will be looked after. If the person who received the property fails to provide that promised care, the Tribunal can declare the transfer void, as though it had been obtained by fraud or coercion.

whatToDo: Keep proof that you cannot support yourself, such as medical records and absence of income, along with proof of your children's or relatives' means.
If you gave away property on a promise of care that was not kept, raise section 23 of the 2007 Act before the Tribunal; do not sign a fresh transfer or settlement without legal advice.
A Hindu parent can choose between the Tribunal under the 2007 Act and a civil suit under the Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956; take advice on which fits your facts.
Apply at the Sub-Divisional Magistrate's office for your area; the Tribunal process does not require hiring a lawyer, though you may still take legal advice.

hi.title: क्या बुज़ुर्ग माता-पिता बच्चों से भरण-पोषण मांग सकते हैं?
keyPoints: जो माता-पिता या वरिष्ठ नागरिक अपना भरण-पोषण स्वयं नहीं कर सकते, वे माता-पिता एवं वरिष्ठ नागरिक भरण-पोषण अधिनियम, 2007 के तहत बच्चों से मासिक भरण-पोषण मांग सकते हैं।
आवेदन सिविल कोर्ट नहीं, बल्कि उपजिलाधिकारी (एसडीएम) की अध्यक्षता वाले भरण-पोषण अधिकरण में दाखिल होता है, जो अधिकतम 10,000 रुपये प्रति माह तक का आदेश दे सकता है।
दावा करने के लिए माता-पिता की उम्र 60 वर्ष होना ज़रूरी नहीं; केवल 'वरिष्ठ नागरिक' के रूप में स्वयं के लिए दावा करने वाले को यह उम्र पूरी करनी होती है।
यदि किसी बच्चे को देखभाल के वादे पर संपत्ति दी गई हो और वह वादा पूरा न करे, तो अधिकरण उस हस्तांतरण को रद्द घोषित कर सकता है।
p: जो माता-पिता अपनी आय या संपत्ति से अपना भरण-पोषण नहीं कर सकते, वे 2007 के अधिनियम की धारा 4 के तहत हल्द्वानी और नैनीताल सहित अपने ज़िले के भरण-पोषण अधिकरण में आवेदन कर सकते हैं, जहाँ अधिकतम भरण-पोषण राशि 10,000 रुपये प्रति माह तक हो सकती है।
